newsitem.title: USA: Texas man convicted for death of fetus.
newsitem.headline: Texas man convicted for death of fetus.

text.p: A Texas man was found guilty on Thursday of killing an unborn child in a drunk driving accident.
Frank Cuellar, 50, faces up to 20 years in jail for the crime of intoxication manslaughter, which was the result of a June 15 car accident, officials said.
Prosecutors said Cuellar had been drinking when he crashed into a car carrying the foetus' mother, who was just over seven months pregnant at the time.
The mother suffered only a broken ankle, but doctors detected signs of stress in the foetus and performed an emergency Cesarean section to deliver the child, Krystal Zuniga.
Krystal's brain was severely injured in the crash and she died 44 hours after birth.
Prosecutors told the jury in opening arguments on Tuesday that they were to decide only Cuellar's guilt or innocence, not the question of when life begins.
But defence attorney Anne Marshall said in closing arguments, "I think the law says that there was no Krystal Zuniga at 11:20 (p.m.)," referring to the time when the accident occurred.
The jury took just 55 minutes to reach its verdict.
Attorneys could not comment on Thursday because of a gag order imposed by State District Judge Robert Blackmon, but Marshall indicated before the trial that she expected to appeal a guilty verdict.
Cuellar, who also was indicted for intoxication assault and driving while intoxicated and could be tried later on those charges, was to be sentenced on Friday.
